summary: The candidate is a substantive partial fix: eager FP8 paged/nonpaged paths now budget and row-chunk the context-proportional logits allocation, graph modes no longer disable budgeting outright, and a budget smaller than one aligned row is rejected. However, graph-backed execution uses only a configuration-derived budget. With the issue's mem_fraction_static=0.9 on an 80 GiB device, that budget is 1.6 GiB, so the issue-sized 1.421875 GiB matrix is not chunked even when live free memory is the reported 1.17 GiB. The original OOM therefore remains possible in graph mode.

tests.what_was_measured: Confirmed the base FP8 paged and nonpaged paths have no memory-budget row planner and computed the reported 4096 x align256(92992) x fp32 allocation as 1526726656 bytes (1.421875 GiB).

Candidate regression suite: 20 passed and 29 subtests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2; actual GPU top-k output matched between unchunked execution and row chunks of 1, 3, 7, 16, and 40.

remaining_counterexamples: Graph-backed execution cannot incorporate unexpectedly low live free memory. With total_memory=80 GiB, mem_fraction_static=0.9, and the default 0.2 logits fraction, the candidate's static graph budget is 1717986918 bytes (1.6 GiB). It therefore leaves the issue-sized 1526726656-byte matrix unchunked although the issue reports only 1.17 GiB free, so that allocation can still OOM.
The full DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 800K-token TP4 H100 serving reproduction remains unverified because the required model weights and CUDA/H100 topology were unavailable.
remaining_limitations: The assigned accelerator was one AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 under ROCm 7.2, not four NVIDIA H100 GPUs under CUDA 12.9.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 weights were unavailable, so no full HTTP/serving-path or 800K-token model run was performed.
The GPU check validates the row-wise top-k equivalence contract, not CUDA DeepGEMM execution or TP4 behavior.
No native source changed in the candidate, so a native rebuild was not applicable. Imports were confirmed to resolve to /job/repo/python/sglang.
